get_person_data.title: Look up a person
get_person_data.description: Query the Pessoas (people) API for one or more datasets about a person. `q` names the key in BigDataCorp's syntax -- `doc{CPF}` for a document number -- and `datasets` is a comma-separated list of dataset technical names such as "basic_data". Every dataset in the list is a billed query, so ask for only what you need.

q.description: The query, in BigDataCorp's key syntax -- e.g. "doc{12345678901}" for a CPF. Queries by name, phone or email may match several people.

datasets.description: Comma-separated dataset technical names, e.g. "basic_data" or "basic_data,addresses". Each one is billed separately.

limit.description: Most entities to return, for a query with no unique key. Maximum 80.

output.description: The matching people, with one block per requested dataset.

get_person_basic_data.title: Get a person's registration data
get_person_basic_data.description: Fetch the `basic_data` dataset for one person -- the registration core (name, document, status and dates). The narrow, cheap version of get_person_data for the most common lookup.

q.description: The query, usually "doc{CPF}" for a document-number lookup.

limit.description: Most entities to return when the query is not a unique key. Maximum 80.

get_company_data.title: Look up a company
get_company_data.description: Query the Empresas (companies) API for one or more datasets about a company. `q` is usually `doc{CNPJ}`; `datasets` names the technical dataset names you want, such as "basic_data". Each dataset is a billed query.

q.description: The query in BigDataCorp's key syntax -- e.g. "doc{12345678000199}" for a CNPJ. A query by company name may match several candidates.

limit.description: Most entities to return for a non-unique query. Maximum 80.

output.description: The matching companies, with one block per requested dataset.

get_company_basic_data.title: Get a company's registration data
get_company_basic_data.description: Fetch the `basic_data` dataset for one company -- CNPJ, legal and trade name, registration status, legal nature and founding date. The narrow version of get_company_data.

limit.description: Most entities to return for a non-unique query. Maximum 80.

output.description: The company's registration data -- TaxIdNumber, OfficialName, TradeName, TaxIdStatus, LegalNature and founding date among them.

get_address_data.title: Look up an address
get_address_data.description: Query the Endereços (addresses) API, which holds geographic and territorial datasets -- municipalities, biomes, protected areas, rural property records, crime statistics. `datasets` names which of them to read.

q.description: The query in BigDataCorp's key syntax for the addresses API.

datasets.description: Comma-separated dataset technical names for the addresses API, e.g. the municipality or protected-area datasets.

output.description: The matching addresses, with one block per requested dataset.

queue_async_query.title: Queue a query for later collection
queue_async_query.description: Submit a query to be run in the background rather than waiting for it. `api` names which API to run it against ("pessoas", "empresas", "enderecos"), and `hooks` optionally gives a url to push the result to. Answers with a QueryId that get_async_query_result collects.

datasets.description: Comma-separated dataset technical names to fetch.

q.description: The query in BigDataCorp's key syntax.

hooks.description: Where to push the result once ready, as BigDataCorp's hook specification string. Omit to poll instead.

output.description: The queued query, with the QueryId to collect it by.

get_async_query_result.title: Collect an asynchronous query
get_async_query_result.description: Read the metadata and result of a queued query by its QueryId. Poll this until the query reports finished, unless you gave a hook url.

output.description: The query's metadata and, once ready, its result.

get_async_query_stats.title: Get asynchronous query statistics
get_async_query_stats.description: Read submission statistics for queued queries -- how many have been sent and their status, optionally narrowed to particular datasets.

datasets.description: Comma-separated dataset technical names to report on.

search_by_domain.description: Aggregate by domain rather than by individual query.

list_batch_jobs.title: List batch jobs
list_batch_jobs.description: Read the batch jobs on the account, with their state and progress. A batch job runs the same query over every row of an input file, which is how large enrichments are done.

show_historical.description: Include finished jobs as well as live ones.

get_batch_job.title: Get a batch job
get_batch_job.description: Read one batch job in detail -- its definition, progress and any row errors.

save_batch_job_definition.title: Create or update a batch job definition
save_batch_job_definition.description: Define a batch job: where the input file is, how it is delimited, which API and datasets to run against each row, and where the output should go. Saving a definition does not start it -- start_batch_job does.

job_id.description: The job's id. Omit to create a new definition.

api_name.description: Which data API each row is queried against.

datasets.description: Comma-separated dataset technical names to fetch per row.

view.description: A saved view to project the result through, from list_views.

input_file_url.description: Url BigDataCorp should read the input file from.

input_file_delimiter.description: Column delimiter in the input file.

input_file_has_header.description: Whether the input file's first row is a header.

input_keys_header.description: Which input columns hold the query keys.

input_file_sample_rate.description: Process only a sample of rows, as a percentage -- for a dry run.

expected_record_count.description: How many rows you expect, so BigDataCorp can validate the file.

output_file_url.description: Where the result file should be written.

output_file_delimiter.description: Column delimiter for the output file.

start_batch_job.title: Start a batch job
start_batch_job.description: Begin executing a saved batch job. Every row of the input file becomes a billed query, so check the definition and the row count first.

pause_batch_job.title: Pause a batch job
pause_batch_job.description: Pause a running batch job. Rows already processed are billed and kept; resume_batch_job picks up where it stopped.

resume_batch_job.title: Resume a batch job
resume_batch_job.description: Continue a paused batch job from the row it stopped at.

cancel_batch_job.title: Cancel a batch job
cancel_batch_job.description: Stop a batch job for good. Rows already processed stay billed, and the job cannot be resumed -- restart_batch_job runs it again from the start.

restart_batch_job.title: Restart a batch job
restart_batch_job.description: Run a batch job again from the first row. Every row is queried and billed a second time, so this is not a cheap retry.

list_monitoring_subscriptions.title: List monitoring subscriptions
list_monitoring_subscriptions.description: Read the queries being monitored for changes, with the datasets and parameters each watches. Monitoring re-runs a query on a schedule and reports when the answer moves.

filter_by_parameters.description: Only subscriptions whose parameters match this string.

get_monitoring_subscription.title: Get a monitoring subscription
get_monitoring_subscription.description: Read one monitoring subscription in detail, or look it up by the API, datasets and parameters it watches.

subscription_id.description: The subscription's id. Use this, or the api/datasets/parameters triple.

api.description: Which data API the subscription watches.

datasets.description: Comma-separated dataset technical names it watches.

enable_monitoring.title: Start monitoring a query
enable_monitoring.description: Begin watching a query for changes. `q` and `datasets` describe what to watch, `api` which data API to run it against, and `subscription_hooks` where changes should be pushed.

datasets.description: Comma-separated dataset technical names to watch.

q.description: The query to watch, in BigDataCorp's key syntax.

view.description: A saved view to project the monitored result through.

query_id.description: Monitor an existing query by its id instead of describing it again.

subscription_hooks.description: Where to push changes, as BigDataCorp's hook specification string.

update_monitoring.title: Update a monitoring subscription
update_monitoring.description: Change which datasets a subscription watches, or where its changes are pushed.

datasets.description: New comma-separated dataset list to watch.

subscription_hooks.description: New hook specification for pushing changes.

disable_monitoring.title: Stop monitoring
disable_monitoring.description: Cancel monitoring subscriptions by id (or by the query they watch). No further change notifications are sent.

subscription_ids.description: Ids of the subscriptions to cancel.

query_ids.description: Cancel by monitored query id instead.

api.description: Narrow the cancellation to this data API.

datasets.description: Narrow the cancellation to these datasets.

parameters.description: Narrow the cancellation to these query parameters.

get_monitoring_history.title: Get the monitoring history
get_monitoring_history.description: Read the log of monitoring runs and the changes they found -- the audit trail behind a change notification.

page_id.description: Page cursor from the previous response.

get_monitoring_differences.title: Compare two monitored results
get_monitoring_differences.description: Diff two results of a monitored query -- what actually changed between them, field by field. Pass either two query ids or the two JSON payloads.

subscription_id.description: The subscription the two results belong to.

json_1.description: The earlier result as a JSON string, instead of a query id.

json_2.description: The later result as a JSON string.

api.description: Which data API the results came from.

output.description: The differences between the two results.

set_monitoring_user_settings.title: Configure monitoring callback credentials
set_monitoring_user_settings.description: Tell BigDataCorp how to authenticate against *your* endpoint when it pushes monitoring changes -- a static token, or an OAuth exchange it should perform first. These are credentials for your own receiver, not for BigDataCorp.

access_token.description: Static access token BigDataCorp should present to your endpoint.

authorization_key.description: Header name to send the authorization value in.

oauth_basic_token.description: Basic token used when fetching an OAuth token from your endpoint.

oauth_public_key.description: OAuth client id (public key) for the token exchange.

oauth_private_key.description: OAuth client secret for the token exchange.

oauth_url.description: Token endpoint BigDataCorp should call to obtain a token.

oauth_content_type.description: Content type for the token request.

oauth_grant_type.description: OAuth grant type for the token request.

oauth_token_field.description: Which field of the token response holds the token.

get_view.title: Get a saved view
get_view.description: Read a saved view -- a named projection over a dataset that trims the response to the fields you actually use, which both batch jobs and monitoring can reference.

api.description: Which data API the view belongs to.

q.description: A query to resolve the view against.

locale.description: Locale for the projected field labels.

query_id.description: An existing query id to read the view for.

create_view.title: Create a saved view
create_view.description: Save a named projection over a dataset, so later queries -- including batch jobs -- can ask for just those fields by name.

api.description: Which data API the view belongs to.

q.description: A sample query the view is built from.

locale.description: Locale for the projected field labels.

query_id.description: An existing query id to build the view from.

scope.description: Scope the view should belong to.

update_view.title: Update a saved view
update_view.description: Change a saved view's projection -- which fields it returns and their labels.

api.description: Which data API the view belongs to.

q.description: A sample query for the updated projection.

locale.description: Locale for the projected field labels.

query_id.description: An existing query id to rebuild the view from.

delete_view.title: Delete a saved view
delete_view.description: Delete a saved view. Batch jobs and monitoring subscriptions that reference it by name stop resolving, so check for those first.

api.description: Which data API the view belongs to.

query_id.description: An existing query id identifying the view.

output.description: Confirmation that the view was deleted.

generate_token.title: Generate an access token
generate_token.description: Mint a new access token from a platform login and password. Unlike every other call here, this authenticates from the body rather than the connection's token -- so it is how a token is bootstrapped or rotated.

login.description: Platform login the token should belong to.

expires.description: Token lifetime, in the units BigDataCorp's token API documents.

output.description: The new token and its id.

list_active_token_ids.title: List active token ids
list_active_token_ids.description: Read which access tokens are currently valid for a login. The audit before revoking anything.

login.description: Platform login to list tokens for.

revoke_token.title: Revoke a token
revoke_token.description: Revoke an access token by its value. Anything using it stops working immediately -- including this connection, if you revoke its own token.

login.description: Platform login the token belongs to.

output.description: Confirmation that the token was revoked.

revoke_token_by_id.title: Revoke a token by id
revoke_token_by_id.description: Revoke an access token by its id rather than its value -- the safer form when you have listed ids with list_active_token_ids and never held the token itself.

login.description: Platform login the token belongs to.

output.description: Confirmation that the token was revoked.
